stances_toward.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Bulgaria is the first obstacle on Skopje's EU path: it has blocked the opening of negotiations since 2020 and, with the 2022 French proposal, requires the constitution to name Bulgarians (Zhelyazkov, Oct 2025: Sofia adds no new condition to the 2022 proposal). Skopje answers with two conditions (rights for Macedonians in Bulgaria; no further bilateral vetoes) and the Commission notes that no steps have been taken. Incidents keep the wound open: the Ivan Mihailov club sentence (Jun 2025), the arson of two Bulgarian embassy cars in Skopje (15 Jun 2026, suspect detained, motive unknown). The grade is rival, not ally, although both are NATO members (the dataset would derive 'ally'): Sofia's claim that Macedonian language and history are Bulgarian is a contest over identity, and the bilateral friendship treaty of 2017 and Corridor 8 are working in parallel. Trend stable: von der Leyen's visit of 2 Oct 2026 produced a first step, but no movement on the constitution. Bond - grievance: history, language, the 1943 Vatasha anniversary a day after the arson.

relations_to.summary: Mickoski says there will be no constitutional amendment adding Bulgarians while he is prime minister unless Bulgaria first guarantees rights for the Macedonian community and the EU guarantees no further bilateral vetoes; on 28 May 2026 he said the government was ready to 'pay the price' of delayed accession. Sofia says it adds no condition to the 2022 proposal.

sources.title: North Macedonia PM Mickoski sets two conditions for constitutional amendments
North Macedonia EU deadlock deepens as Mickoski hardens stance, opposition demands referendum
PM Zhelyazkov: Bulgaria is not setting new conditions for Republic of North Macedonia's EU path

relations_to.summary: Skopje's first condition for any amendment is that the Macedonian community in Bulgaria receives the rights guaranteed by international law and human-rights conventions; Mickoski said he was not asking for a change to Bulgaria's constitution. Foreign minister Mucunski in April 2026 asked for 'minimal reciprocity'.

sources.title: North Macedonia PM Mickoski sets two conditions for constitutional amendments
North Macedonia FM sets conditions for progress with Bulgaria, citing trust and 'reciprocity'

relations_to.summary: Treaty of Friendship, Good Neighbourliness and Cooperation signed in August 2017 and ratified by Bulgaria on 18 January 2018, with a protocol and a joint commission on historical and educational issues; the Commission asks both sides to implement it in good faith.

sources.title: North Macedonia 2025 Report (regional relations: Treaty of Friendship, Good Neighbourliness and Cooperation)
Foreign relations of North Macedonia (index: friendship treaty of August 2017, ratified 18 January 2018)

relations_to.summary: Two vehicles with diplomatic plates were set on fire in front of the Bulgarian embassy in Skopje on 15 Jun 2026; a 44-year-old suspect was detained and has admitted the act (Mickoski), motive unknown. Bulgarian President Iotova called it an attack on Bulgaria; Mickoski condemned it.

sources.title: Arson of Diplomatic Cars Adds to Bulgaria-North Macedonia Strains
Bulgarian associations in North Macedonia condemn Skopje arson attack on Bulgarian embassy diplomatic vehicles

relations_to.summary: President Siljanovska-Davkova met Bulgarian President Iotova in Sofia on 10 Jun 2026 on the sidelines of the South-East European Cooperation Process summit; she said Sofia's concerns went beyond the amendments to history and the joint history commission, and Mucunski asked for assurances of no further demands.

sources.title: Arson of Diplomatic Cars Adds to Bulgaria-North Macedonia Strains

relations_to.summary: Ljupcho Georgievski, head of the banned Ivan Mihailov Cultural Club in Bitola and a dual citizen, received a one-year suspended sentence (two years' probation) in June 2025 for quoting Mihailov on social media; Bulgaria's foreign minister called it 'categorically unacceptable' and a protest was held outside the Macedonian embassy in Sofia. The 2023 law bans organisations named after figures the state deems controversial.
